subject: basic embeddable widget (by Sage) works in shiny app

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: basic embeddable widget (by Sage) works in shiny app
parts:
Just saw this post on embeddable widget (by Sage) to run R (or python, or ...) in a webpage. Just for fun I wanted to see it this would work by just pasting the commands in the post to a js file and sourcing that file in ui.R with includeHTML(). It does! Very cool indeed. See sage-tab in the gist linked below.

Something like this for shiny/knitr/R would be amazing. http://glimmer.rstudio.com/yihui/knitr/ by Yihui looks to be moving in this direction as well. Running on a remote server might be a security problem but for local analysis this could be really useful!

http://statisfactions.com/2013/interactive-r-code-widget/

https://gist.github.com/4436647

shiny::runGist('4436647')

messages.subject: Re: basic embeddable widget (by Sage) works in shiny app
parts:
This is also my wish, and I'd love to see how the idea of embedded R
cells goes, but Shiny may not be the appropriate backend in this case;
at most you can embed a Shiny app in <iframe> in another page. OpenCPU
has the better potential to do this but it does not support a
persistent R session, as far as I can see. Maybe I'm wrong, and you
are welcome to explore along this idea further :)

Regards,
Yihui

Sorry I did not make myself clear. I mean I do not see the possibility
of running the Shiny R cell in another web server which does not have
R, i.e. you can only run it in your own server. By comparison, OpenCPU
allows you to call R from an arbitrary place (not necessarily in
OpenCPU's web pages).

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: basic embeddable widget (by Sage) works in shiny app
parts:
Yes, we can use POST, and the.other.server.com must support "Cross
Origin Resource Sharing", and that is one thing critical. This problem
does not exist if Shiny and the web page are on the same server.

You can write a textarea, say, in your blog post, and POST it to
OpenCPU and get the results back, but you cannot do that with Shiny
unless Shiny is actively running behind your blog. That is my
understanding.

What I'm saying is "embeddable anywhere" (thinking OpenCPU API), and
your example shows "embeddable cells in your app".

Regards,
Yihui
